title: RBAC: add dual-evaluation mode (v1 + v2) with shadow-deny metrics + dashboards
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes:
- Control plane now supports RBAC dual-evaluation (v1 enforced, v2 shadow) behind feature flags.
- New metrics/logging fields emitted for v2 shadow denies (and allow/deny diffs) to support safe migration.
- Grafana dashboard added for shadow-deny rate, top endpoints, and top reason codes by org/service.
- No behavior changes by default; enforcement of v2 remains gated.
description:
Context: We need a safe path to migrate from RBAC v1 (feature-gated + inconsistent checks) to RBAC v2 (resource/action/scope + policy bundles). This PR adds a dual-evaluation mode where we continue to enforce v1, but also evaluate v2 in parallel and emit metrics/log context for any discrepancies (esp. v2 deny when v1 allowed). This enables staged rollout with low risk of accidentally breaking enterprise admin/support workflows.

What’s included: Add dual-eval plumbing in control-plane auth middleware (evaluate v1 first for decision; evaluate v2 as shadow based on flags); Standardize “shadow result” telemetry (counters + histograms + structured log fields); Add aggregation labels needed for dashboards (service, route, method, action, resource, org_id hashed, actor_type, reason_code); Add Grafana dashboard JSON + runbook notes for interpreting shadow-deny metrics; Add sampling + cardinality guards to avoid metric explosions; Add unit + integration tests to ensure dual-eval does not change enforcement behavior.

Design notes: v1 remains the source of truth for allow/deny while dual-eval is enabled; v2 evaluation is best-effort: failures do not impact request outcome but are surfaced via metrics (eval_error); “shadow deny” is defined as (v1=allow && v2=deny) — this is the primary signal for migration risk; “shadow allow” (v1=deny && v2=allow) is tracked but lower priority (often indicates missing v1 grants or legacy gates). Telemetry is emitted only when dual-eval flag is enabled for the org or globally for staging.

Flags: rbacv2.dual_eval.enabled (global) and rbacv2.dual_eval.org_allowlist (per-org). Also supports “dryrun-only” mode in staging for all orgs with sampling.

Testing: Added unit tests around comparison matrix (allow/deny/error permutations). Added integration tests for representative endpoints (API keys, org settings) that assert response remains identical while shadow telemetry increments.

Rollout: Staging: enable globally with 10% sampling; Production: enable for internal dogfood orgs first, then enterprise canary orgs. Use dashboard to identify top shadow-deny endpoints and update policy bundle/role mappings before moving to v2 enforcement.

Linked: ENG-5389 (Migration plan implementation), ENG-5381 (RBAC v2 project).
commits: authz/metrics: add shadow comparison counters + latency histograms
logging: propagate authz decision context fields (shadow)
config: add dual-eval flags + org allowlist support
tests: add v1/v2 comparison table tests
snippet:
Illustrative change (middleware):

Before:
- decision := v1.Enforce(ctx, req)
- if !decision.Allowed { return 403 }
- next()

After:
- v1Decision := v1.Enforce(ctx, req)
- if dualEvalEnabled(org) {
    v2Decision, v2Err := v2.Evaluate(ctx, req)
    emitShadowTelemetry(v1Decision, v2Decision, v2Err, labels...)
    attachShadowFieldsToLogs(ctx, v2Decision, v2Err)
  }
- if !v1Decision.Allowed { return 403 }
- next()
review_conversation:
Kaitlyn Nguyen (requested changes): The metrics look right, but I’m worried about label cardinality. org_id in labels is going to explode even if hashed. Can we remove org_id from default labels and only include it in structured logs? Also, please confirm that v2 eval failures don’t change response codes.

Connor O'Brien (author): Agreed. I removed org_id from metrics labels entirely; we keep org_id_hash in logs only. Metrics now aggregate by service/route/action/reason_code/actor_type. v2 errors are treated as shadow eval_error; v1 enforcement remains the sole decision.

Jordan Lee (comment): For discrepancies, can we also emit a “v2_action_missing” reason when an endpoint doesn’t declare an action? That’s been a common source of denies in dev.

Connor O'Brien: Added explicit reason_code mapping: ACTION_UNDECLARED, POLICY_MISS, SCOPE_MISMATCH, EXPLICIT_DENY, EVAL_ERROR. ACTION_UNDECLARED is incremented for shadow denies when the v2 resolver can’t map route->action.

Allison Grant (comment): Please ensure logs have stable field names for downstream parsing. Suggest: authz.v1.decision, authz.v2.shadow.decision, authz.v2.shadow.reason_code, authz.policy_version.

Connor O'Brien: Updated fields to match the logging standard. Also added a short section in the dashboard README describing how to pivot on reason_code.

Sean Gallagher (comment): From SRE side, we need a dashboard panel showing “shadow denies by endpoint over time” and a top-N list. Also alerting threshold suggestions?

Connor O'Brien: Added 3 panels: (1) shadow deny rate, (2) top endpoints by shadow denies, (3) top reason codes. Added suggested alerts as commented examples (not enabled) in README since we don’t want paging from this yet.

Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Thanks for keeping enforcement unchanged and isolating the extra work behind the allowlist flag. Please follow up with a PR to add this middleware to the console backend after control-plane bake.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (approval): Approved after label changes + tests. This will help a lot for migration confidence.
